label: r215 -- containers for five prose-derived headline figures. Nothing new measured.
method: dose_r174.py formula incl. excitation clamp; cycles_in() imported from analyse_ladder_r169.py, definitions-only exec

fig1_avoidance_vs_specified.quantity: achieved delivered dose MINUS the dose the lesion SPECIFIES, as a percentage of specified. NOT the same quantity as fig2.
fig1_avoidance_vs_specified.operationalisation: specified = KV*max(0,ce_vel_norm) evaluated on the CONTROL arm's kinematics (what the lesion would deliver to an unadapted gait); achieved = the same formula on the SPASTIC arm's own kinematics

fig2_avoidance_vs_control_arm.quantity: spastic arm delivered dose MINUS the CONTROL arm's delivered dose, as a percentage of control. NOT the same quantity as fig1.
fig2_avoidance_vs_control_arm.cells: R203V* speed-study cells -- DISJOINT from fig1's r151/r174 cells
fig2_avoidance_vs_control_arm.excluded: cmd_1.30 gives -26.27 % -- the CONTROL arm speeds up there, so the denominator moves and the level is not comparable

fig1_and_fig2_are_different_quantities.statement: fig1 is achieved-versus-SPECIFIED on the r151/r174 cells; fig2 is spastic-versus-CONTROL-ARM on the disjoint r203 cells. Two operationalisations, two cell sets, no shared data.
fig1_and_fig2_are_different_quantities.why_it_matters: RETRACTED r216. The former text read 'agreement from disjoint cells under different operationalisations is stronger than one measure repeated'. That is WITHDRAWN. The underlying quantities agree to 0.05-0.10 % (references) and 0.12-0.13 % (achieved), so the two operationalisations produce the same four numbers: this is the SAME CONTRAST REPLICATED ON A SECOND CORPUS, not triangulation from two directions. Replication guards against a corpus-specific artefact; it does not guard against a shared error in the dose computation, which both use.
fig1_and_fig2_are_different_quantities.retraction_note: The header of RESULTS_3d_r214.md gives the deposit precedence over the prose. The retraction is therefore made HERE, not only in the prose.

fig3_dose_line.quantity: delivered dose per unit gait speed at fixed KV = 0.050
fig3_dose_line.arithmetic: slope = dose_N / speed_mps (a line through the origin: the velocity term scales with fibre velocity, which time-scaling makes proportional to speed)

confirmation.note: NOT summarised as a tolerance. The four per-arm errors and the span are deposited; the summary was the thing that lost information.
confirmation.span_confirmed: a 0.50 m/s commanded change produced +0.075 m/s in control -- 15 % of intent. The line is confirmed over 15 % of the intended span and no further.

fig4_speed_ceiling.quantity: highest gait speed reached from the registered warm start, at triple budget
fig4_speed_ceiling.arithmetic: mean of the final speed over the depth-probe cells
fig4_speed_ceiling.why_a_ceiling_not_a_shortfall: 270 further generations bought +0.037, +0.031 m/s -- monotone and still creeping, i.e. asymptotic rather than unconverged
fig4_speed_ceiling.precision_warning: result_mps is the mean of TWO cells (n=2) whose values differ by ~0.004 m/s and which why_a_ceiling_not_a_shortfall records as still gaining at generation ~270. Quoting it to five significant figures overstates it; 1.13 m/s is what n=2 supports.

fig5_provocation_over_usable_span.quantity: extra delivered dose obtainable by walking at the ceiling instead of baseline
fig5_provocation_over_usable_span.comparison: the controller removes 20.5 % of its own dose (fig2); speed can add 10.3 %

derived_channel_warning.claim: as_pct_of_baseline_dose is ALGEBRAICALLY IDENTICAL to inputs.usable_span_pct and carries no information beyond fig4 and the baseline.
derived_channel_warning.why: fig3 is declared a line through the origin, so delivered dose is proportional to speed. A percentage of baseline dose is therefore identically a percentage of baseline speed: slope*(ceiling-baseline) / (slope*baseline) = (ceiling-baseline)/baseline. The slope cancels.
derived_channel_warning.never_quote_as: These two must NEVER be quoted as agreeing measurements. They are one measurement written twice.
derived_channel_warning.tail_difference: 10.315327407006656 vs 10.315327407006654 differ in the SEVENTEENTH significant digit. It is floating-point operation ordering, NOT a discrepancy, and must not be reported as one.
derived_channel_warning.class: This is the parallelism error one level up -- a derived channel sitting beside its parent where a reader takes the agreement as corroboration. MATCHED_RESULT_r174.md section 0 records the same class for gait channels; it recurred inside the deposit built to prevent it. Found by the coordinator recomputing the deposit rather than by the seat that wrote it.

extrapolation_warning.claim: result_N = 1.4056 applies the fig3 slope out to a ceiling of 1.126872 m/s.
extrapolation_warning.but: fig3.confirmation.span_confirmed records that the line is confirmed over 15 % of the intended span and no further: a 0.50 m/s commanded change produced +0.075 m/s in control.
extrapolation_warning.therefore: 1.4056 N is an EXTRAPOLATION past the last validated speed, not an interpolation within a confirmed range. It must not be quoted without that qualification.

prose_vs_regenerated.what_this_block_is: A record of a SUPERSEDED DRAFT's numbers checked against the regenerated values. The 'quoted' fields are the OLD draft's figures. They are NOT what the shipping prose says.
prose_vs_regenerated.ok_false_is_not_a_live_error: ok:false marks a draft value that WAS WRONG AND WAS CORRECTED BEFORE SHIPPING. RESULTS_3d_r214.md carries the 'regenerated' values, not the 'quoted' ones: it says 1.4056 N and 10.32 %, not 1.47 and 11.0. A referee should read ok:false as 'caught and fixed', not as an outstanding discrepancy.
prose_vs_regenerated.shipping_prose_carries: the regenerated column, in every row

fig5_provocation_N.⛔ DISCREPANCY: the quoted 1.47 N is 13.340 * (1.13 - 1.02) -- BOTH ENDPOINTS ROUNDED BEFORE SUBTRACTING. The exact endpoints give 13.3398 * (1.126872 - 1.021501) = 1.4056 N. Rounding a difference of two near-equal rounded numbers inflated it by 4.6 %, in the direction that made the speed axis look more viable than it is.

usable_span_pct.note: same cause: 1.13/1.02 rounded before the ratio

r217_severity_independence.claim_that_would_have_shipped: The spastic-weak speed gap is three to four times larger than the entire weakness severity range can produce -- gap 0.0445-0.0578 m/s against a ladder span of 0.0133 m/s.
r217_severity_independence.refuted_by: PREREG_window_r218.md, recomputing on the G2 window [1.00, 9.73]
r217_severity_independence.on_the_uncircular_window: gap 0.0068 m/s against a ladder span 0.0078 m/s -- THE SAME ORDER, not three to four times.
r217_severity_independence.why_the_first_was_wrong: The 13.58 s window's upper bound is the shortest admitted spastic cell's termination time, so the spastic arm was measured partly on its approach to failure. The G2 bound of 9.73 s is a fixed fraction of a benchmark measured before any of these cells existed.
r217_severity_independence.what_is_supported_now: REINSTATED, with its metric named: on a MEAN-TO-MEAN basis the spastic-weak gap is 3.4-4.4x the entire weakness severity span, on BOTH windows. On an EXTREME-VALUE basis the margin is 1.36x (13.58) and 0.88x (G2) -- the same order as the span. BOTH are true and they answer different questions: mean-gap asks whether the arms' centres are far apart relative to severity; margin asks whether the distributions overlap. The disjointness claim (6 cells vs 36, no overlap, both windows) is the extreme-value statement and stands separately.
r217_severity_independence.STATUS: RETRACTION REVERSED r220 -- the claim is REINSTATED, and the stated cause was false.
r217_severity_independence.why_the_retraction_was_wrong: The retraction compared a MEAN-TO-MEAN gap (0.0445-0.0578, the 13.58 window) against an EXTREME-VALUE MARGIN (0.0068, the G2 window) and attributed the difference to the window. Computed like-for-like the r217 claim SURVIVES: mean-gap is 3.36-4.36x on the data-chosen window and 3.49-4.49x on the uncircular one. The window did not refute it; switching metric did.
r217_severity_independence.history_kept_visible: r217 claimed 3-4x. r218 retracted it citing the window. r220 found the retraction's cause false, reinstated the claim, and named the metric. All three states are recorded here deliberately.

correlation_spastic_speed_vs_duration.note: Descriptive only. Six pairs; no p-value is quoted and none may be.
correlation_spastic_speed_vs_duration.coefficients_are_uninformative: A Pearson of +0.372 on SIX pairs has a confidence interval spanning roughly -0.6 to +0.9. It cannot distinguish no relationship from a substantial one. The coefficients are retained so a reader sees them and sees why they carry no weight; they must NOT be quoted as evidence that speed is independent of duration. An earlier version read them as reassurance, which is a null claimed from an underpowered estimate -- the same shape this project rejected when six Gate-G failures were read as 'no data'.
correlation_spastic_speed_vs_duration.what_the_six_pairs_DO_support: WITHDRAWN r225. This field previously asserted a falsification: that the SHORTEST cell (13.58 s) was the FASTEST and the second-shortest the SLOWEST, contradicting a monotone termination artefact. THAT ORDERING HOLDS ONLY ON THE DATA-CHOSEN WINDOW. On the uncircular G2 window (WINDOW_G2_r218.json -> arms.'spastic KV 0.050'.per_seed) the shortest cell, seed 103 at 13.58 s, is 1.0201 m/s while the LONGEST, seed 101 at 17.85 s, is the FASTEST at 1.0242 m/s -- which is the termination-artefact ordering the argument claimed to refute. The falsification is withdrawn; no mechanism is ruled out.
correlation_spastic_speed_vs_duration.withdrawal_note: Withdrawn in the DEPOSIT and not only in the prose. RESULTS_3d_r214.md's header gives the deposit precedence, so a withdrawal made only in prose leaves the refuted claim standing as the authority. This file already carried that lesson at figures.fig1_and_fig2_are_different_quantities.retraction_note and it was not applied here.
correlation_spastic_speed_vs_duration.consequence_for_the_13_58_window: With the falsification withdrawn, the termination-artefact reading is LIVE again for every speed number measured on [1.00, 13.58]. PREREG_window_r218.md section 4 registered that this must be stated wherever a speed number appears, independently of how the window test came out.

metric_by_window_2x2.what: Gap-to-ladder-span ratio under BOTH metrics and BOTH windows. Paths: SPEED_LADDER_r217.json and WINDOW_G2_r218.json -> arms.*.mean_speed_mps / max_speed_mps / min_speed_mps.
metric_by_window_2x2.conclusion: THE RATIO TRACKS THE METRIC, NOT THE WINDOW. Mean-gap gives 3.4-4.4x on BOTH windows; extreme-margin gives 1.36x and 0.88x on both. Switching window changes the ratio by ~4 %; switching metric changes it by ~4x.
